question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Amazon)

calls.reasoning: Consensus Q3 2026 EPS ~$2.00 (range 1.95-2.03); guide OI $22.5-26.5B. Amazon beat top of OI guide by $3.5B in Q2 2026 (27.5B vs 20-24B) and ex-gain EPS 1.97 vs 1.86 est; similar beat implies OI ~29-30B and EPS ~2.05-2.20. Reported GAAP EPS in Q1 (2.78) and Q2 (5.75) were inflated by Anthropic gains from Feb and May priced rounds; in Q3 the only Anthropic transaction found is a $15B credit facility (debt) and the IPO is slated for November, so a big mark-up gain is unlikely but not impossible (~7% upper escape). Non-operating Rivian/equity swings add noise. No human market (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold) found.

- Status quo: earnings near consensus with operating beat; no market (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold) found.
- Event window: Q3 2026 report released ~Oct 28-29, 2026; resolves on that release.

calls.reasoning: Resolves on Q3 2026 diluted GAAP EPS (report ~Oct 29). Consensus excluding gains is $1.96-2.03. Op income guidance is $22.5-26.5B and Amazon beat the top by $3.5B in Q2, implying core EPS ~2.05-2.20. GAAP EPS was inflated in Q1 ($2.78) and Q2 ($5.75) by Anthropic gains tied to priced rounds (Feb, May). No Q3 priced Anthropic equity event was found, only $15B of debt, with the IPO aimed at Nov (Q4). So I put ~10% on a gain-driven escape above $2.995 and ~1% below $0.995. calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: consensus ~$1.96-2.03, op income guidance $22.5-26.5B, Q2 beat, Anthropic gains tied to the Feb and May priced rounds, no Q3 priced equity event (only a $15B credit facility), IPO in ~Nov. They differ only in judgment about upper-escape mass (7%/15%/13%) and slightly in the lower tail. No web access on this run, so I could not check further. The absence of a Q3 priced event was searched by all three runs and not found, which argues against 15%. Unannounced milestone-tranche investments or secondary-transaction marks under the measurement alternative are still possible, so I took 10%. I kept the runs' core median of ~2.10 and widened the lower tail slightly for non-operating losses (Rivian, energy derivatives). I carried forward the runs' reference class and dispersion, which I agree with.
